This petition has been filed under Section 482 of Cr.PC challenging the order dated 10.01.2024 (Annexure A-2) by which learned Additional Session Judge, (FTFC) (POCSO Act), Ramanujganj,
District - Balrampur- Ramanujgan, (CG) has rejected the application of petitioner filed under Section 311 of Cr.PC seeking recall of the victim for cross- examination.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that victim was examined before trial Court on 01.11.2022, but she needs to be re-examined as she could not be cross-examined with respect to her age.

He further submits that during pendency of trial, both the parties have arrived at compromise and an application for compounding the offence has also been filed but the same came to be rejected on 25.11.2023 on the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18502 ground that Sections 363, 366, 376 (2)(n)
of IPC and Section 5(i) & 6 of the POCSO are non-compoundable in nature.

He submits that the application was moved under Section 311 CrPC for recalling the victim in order to bring on record correct facts and circumstances, which could not be elicited during cross-examination of victim and are also material for just disposal of the trial.
However, the trial Court by the impugned order has erroneously rejected the said application.

He submits that the trial Court has vide power under Section 311 CrPC to recall and re- examine the witness at any time, therefore, the trial Court ought to Asruddin Ansari vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12834008/
1 have allowed the application filed on behalf of application under Section 311 of CrPC for recalling the victim.

sentences.text: He submits that rejection of application in the given facts and circumstances of the case would amount to failure of justice and it would also amount to abuse of process of the Court.

3. Learned State Counsel opposing the submission of counsel for the petitioner would submit that victim, who is sought to be recalled for re- examination, was already examined and cross-examined extensively by counsel for the defence.
There is no sufficient ground to recall the aforesaid witness.
The learned trial court has rightly rejected the said application for recall of the victim.

4. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused the deposition of victim placed on record.
5.
From perusal of the order impugned it is reflecting that re-examination of the victim is sought on the point of her date of birth.

The trial Court rejected the application for re-examination on the ground that in Para 9 Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18502 & 10 of the cross-examination, the victim has been cross-examined in detail with respect to her age and date of birth and as such, the application filed on behalf of applicant is baseless.
This apart, the trial Court has also recorded that the application is filed at belated stage, whereas applicant is in custody and the matter is to be decided at the earliest.
6. Deposition sheet of victim is placed on record along with covering memo dated 31.05.2024.

Perusal of the deposition sheet of the victim reveals that counsel appearing on behalf of applicant has been afforded reasonable opportunity to cross-examine the victim and he has also duly cross-examined the victim on almost all points.

Para-10 of the cross-examination of victim reveals that she has specifically denied the suggestion that at the time of her admission in Class 1 st, her age was 9- 10 years; she has admitted that she has Aadhar Car in which her date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.2002.
7.

Thus, filing of application for re-examination of the victim after rejection of application for compounding of offence by trial Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18502 Court, is indicative of the fact that the victim has been win over by the applicant and to record favourable statement, the application for recalling her has been filed by the accused on the ground that victim could not be examined in detail on the point of her age, which cannot be allowed as no ground exists in terms of Section 311 CrPC.
8.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down the some guidelines in the case of Natasha Singh vs. CBI (State), reported in 2013 (5) SCC 741 has held as under :

sentences.text: The scope and object of the provision is to enable the Court to determine the truth and to render a just decision after discovering all relevant facts and obtaining proper proof of such facts, to arrive at a just decision of the case.
Power must be exercised judiciously and not capriciously or arbitrarily, as any improper or capricious exercise of such power may lead to undesirable results.

An application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. must not be allowed only to fill up a lacuna in the case of the prosecution, or of the defence, or to the disadvantage of the accused, or to cause serious prejudice to the defence of the accused, or to give an unfair advantage to the opposite party.
Further, the additional evidence must not be received as a disguise for retrial, or to change the nature of the case against either of the parties.
Such a power must be exercised, provided that the evidence that is likely to be tendered by a witness, is germane to the issue involved.
An opportunity of rebuttal however, must be given to the other party.

The power conferred under Section 311 Cr.P.C. must therefore, be invoked by the Court only in order to meet the ends of justice, for strong and valid reasons, and the same must be exercised with great caution and circumspection.

The very use of words such as 'any Court', 'at any stage', or any enquiry, trial or other proceedings', 'any person' and 'any such person' clearly spells out that the provisions of this section have been expressed in the widest possible terms, and do not limit the discretion of the Court in any way.
There is thus no Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18502 escape if the fresh evidence to be obtained is essential to the just decision of the case.
The determinative factor should therefore be, whether the summoning/recalling of the said witness is in fact, essential to the just decision of the case."
(emphasis supplied)

9. Therefore, in view of the principle laid down in above decision and in the given facts and circumstances of case, particularly statement of victim, in the opinion of this Court, no ground exists in terms of Section 311 CrPC to recall the victim for cross examination.
There is no illegality in the order impugned by which the trial Court rejected application of applicant filed under Section 311 CrPC.
10. The petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
